Lemma
[Parabolic scaling of heat balls] \group Heat Equation ↗ def:heat-ball

Assume $n \geq 1$ and $r>0$. Under the parabolic dilation \[ (y,s) \longmapsto (x+ry,t+r^2s), \] the unit heat ball $E(0,0;1)$ is mapped bijectively onto $E(x,t;r)$, and for every $(y,s) \in E(0,0;1)$ (so $s<0$) the Watson weight obeys \[ \frac{|x-(x+ry)|^2}{(t-(t+r^2s))^2} = r^{-2}\frac{|y|^2}{s^2}. \]
Proof

For the positive elapsed time $\tau =-s$ and $z=-y$, the Gaussian satisfies the scaling identity $\Phi (rz,r^2\tau )=r^{-n}\Phi (z,\tau )$. Substitution in the defining inequalities therefore gives the membership equivalence; the explicit inverse dilation proves the set equality, and the bijectivity declaration supplies the corresponding one-to-one correspondence. The weight identity follows by cancelling the factors $r^2$ in the numerator and denominator.

□
